detail_shards.filename_rule: detail-<safe_id>.json where safe_id is the component id with '/' replaced by '--' and ':' replaced by '__'. Example: component id 'viewer/src' -> data/detail-viewer--src.json.
detail_shards.index: component_detail_index (in manifest.json) maps component id -> {symbolCount, fileCount}

endpoints.contains: The structural entry document: components (nested), relationships, stats, and every optional section listed under `manifest_sections`. Fetch this first for any structural question. Excludes the heavy per-symbol/per-file arrays (those live in the detail shards).
Per-component depth: {symbols: [...], files: [...]}. Fetch only for the component you are drilling into. See `detail_shards.filename_rule`.

manifest_sections.contains: Component tree (nested via `children`); each node carries id, name, path, type, files, relationships refs, and optional `ai_enhance`.
Flat list of edges between components (source, target, type; optional `evidence`, `confidence`, `origin`, `ai_enhance`).
Roll-up counts: total_components, total_files, total_lines, total_symbols, total_relationships, languages.
Manifest-embedded coverage summary (counts per disposition + total + parsed). Full ledger with per-file rows and non-source inventory is in coverage.json.
Manifest-embedded activity summary (hotspots/knowledge headline). Full activity lens is in activity.json.
Ranked flat list of findings (rule violations, duplication, intent conformance, AI-verified issues). Filter by `category`/`title`/`severity`.
Flat list of concerns (named cross-cutting groupings of findings).
Flat index of detected capabilities (web/CLI frameworks and features).
Flat index of data entities (models, schemas, tables).
Flat index of which components read/write which data entities.
Flat index of project rules and their pass/violation state.
Guided walkthroughs (ordered component sequences) when present.
Architecture-level AI overlay (description, help text, provenance markers) when the dataset is enriched.
Ordered projection changelog entries (what changed since the previous projection).
Map of component id -> {symbolCount, fileCount}; sizes the per-component detail shards before you fetch them.

token_economy.principle: Fetch the smallest set of files that answers the question. Never crawl the whole tree. The point of this projection is to answer questions about the codebase in a fraction of the tokens that reading the raw source would cost.
rules: Start at manifest.json (split) or architecture.json (monolith) for any structural question.
For findings/concerns/coverage-summary/activity-summary, the manifest often answers in a single fetch; do not pull shards.
For a name/path lookup, use the search shards, then fetch at most one detail shard for depth.
Detail shards are per-component: fetch only the component you are drilling into, never the whole data/ directory.
Treat each fetch as a cost; prefer the manifest's embedded summaries over the full coverage.json / activity.json unless you need per-row detail.

steps.then: Read stats for scale, then the components tree (nested) for structure. To rank components by importance use activity.json hotspots and/or each component's ai_enhance.criticality when enriched, plus relationship fan-in.
Read .findings (already ranked) and .concerns. Filter by category/title/severity. This is one fetch; do not pull shards.

walk_orders.question: look up a symbol, file, or component by name

steps.then: This dataset has no search index. Walk the components tree (names and paths) and component_detail_index, then fetch the matching detail shard via detail_shards.filename_rule.

walk_orders.question: find the component that owns a file path

steps.then: This dataset has no search index. Walk the components tree (names and paths) and component_detail_index, then fetch the matching detail shard via detail_shards.filename_rule.
Read .coverage for the headline disposition counts (one fetch may be enough).
Only if you need per-file dispositions or the non-source inventory: read .summary, .rows, and .inventory.

walk_orders.question: explore flows and structure in depth

steps.then: Walk .components and .relationships; follow `target_view` and composition edges. Read .tours if present for curated walkthroughs.
Drill into a specific component's symbols and files as needed, one component at a time.
